title: {MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR} template used by scenario but never documented in SKILL.md's substitution contract
evidence: Scenario line 23: `  desired_move_in_date: "{MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR}"` — but SKILL.md's runner substitution lists (step 4, line 172 and template section, line 278) document only: `   - \`{MOVE_IN_DATE}\` → today + 90 days as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. \`date -v+90d +%F\`)` and `- \`{MOVE_IN_DATE}\` — today + 90 days (YYYY-MM-DD, computed at fill time)...`. A repo-wide grep of .claude/skills/ finds MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR only in this scenario file.
detail: The runner substitutes only documented templates, so the literal `{MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR}` posts unsubstituted and fails date parsing — the scenario passes on the parse-failure branch it explicitly disclaims, silently ceasing to pin the 12-month upper bound. SKILL.md:278's 'pin literal dates' claim is also now stale.
recommended_fix: Document `{MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR}` (today + 13 months, e.g. date -v+13m +%F) in SKILL.md's step-4 substitution list and template-variables section; correct line 278's stale literal-dates claim.

title: Stepper gating primitives mirrored from apply_analytics.js guarded only by a KEEP-IN-SYNC comment, no parity check
detail: The stepper's advance-gate and the funnel's completion rule must stay semantically identical, yet nothing automated cross-checks the two implementations (each node test imports only its own module). House convention for mirrors is a parity test (listing_source_options vs is_valid_listing_source).
recommended_fix: Add a node parity test that feeds identical DOM fixtures through both modules' isVisibleRequired/controlSatisfied (and the radio-group rule) and asserts agreement, preserving the no-module-imports constraint.
